brief.headline: Kilitch is a 100% trader in the grey distress zone (Altman Z 1.58, score 2/10) — lead with supply security and qualifying a second source, then ask for 60-day terms (they pay suppliers at 105d) to free ₹5.36 L working capital.

priceAsk.summary: No aggressive price cut — they are a reseller (100.0% traded revenue) carrying a margin, and their 2.8% net margin is wafer-thin.
priceAsk.target: Benchmark to a manufacturer like Manjushree or Mold-Tek to understand the reseller premium, but do not squeeze price hard given distress risk.
priceAsk.basis: Their revenue mix is 100.0% traded, so their price includes a reseller margin. With an Altman Z of 1.58 (grey zone) and Probe score 2/10, a hard price push risks tipping a fragile supplier.

paymentTermAsk.summary: Move from 30 Days After Receipt to 60 days — they already pay their own suppliers at 105d vs peer median 57d, so extending our credit is only fair.
paymentTermAsk.cashImpact: ₹5.36 L working capital freed if we move to 30-day terms (already captured); an additional ₹2.68 L freed if we gain 15 more days (45d total), and further upside to 60d.

brief.financialLeverage: Kilitch's financials are weak: -5.1% EBITDA margin, 2.8% net margin (just below peer 3.1%), return on capital 2.5% (peer 12.0%), Probe42 score 2/10, and Altman Z 1.58 (grey/distress zone). They have pending legal case(s). However, debt is moderate (0.40x) and interest coverage is strong (89.99x), and they generate ₹17.39 Cr free cash flow. Our ₹65.27 L spend is 1.19% of their ₹54.69 Cr revenue — meaningful but not dominant. Their 100.0% traded revenue mix and slim margin mean we should press payment terms and supply continuity, not price.

evidence.point: Kilitch is entirely a trader, not a manufacturer — their price includes a reseller margin
They are in the Altman grey zone, signaling potential distress
Probe42 flags them as high financial risk
They stretch their own payables far beyond the peer median
evidence.figure: Their payable days 105d vs peer median 57d

evidence.point: Our spend is a real revenue share for them
evidence.figure: ₹65.27 L is 1.19% of their ₹54.69 Cr revenue

evidence.point: Margins are razor-thin — deep price cuts risk their viability

alternates.name: Manjushree Technopack Ltd
alternates.why: India's largest rigid-plastic converter at ₹2569.83 Cr revenue, health B (65/100) — top second-source for pharma bottles and caps, far more robust than Kilitch.

alternates.name: Mold-Tek Packaging Ltd
alternates.why: Listed leader in rigid plastic (₹946.50 Cr revenue, health A 79/100) — strong, profitable alternate for bottles and closures.

alternates.name: Hitech Corporation Ltd
alternates.why: Listed moulded packaging player (₹701.17 Cr revenue, health C 57/100) — broad capability across bottles and caps.

risks: Kilitch's Altman Z of 1.58 (grey zone) and Probe score 2/10 mean supply continuity is at risk — do not over-concentrate volume here.
Pending legal case(s) and negative EBITDA margin (-5.1%) suggest operational or financial stress — monitor closely and have Manjushree or Mold-Tek ready.
They are 100.0% a trader, so any manufacturer alternate (Manjushree, Mold-Tek) will likely offer better pricing by cutting out the reseller margin.
Their 2.8% net margin leaves almost no room for a price cut — pushing too hard on price may force them to walk or fail, leaving us scrambling for supply.
brief.suggestedOpeningLine: We value the partnership, but given your Probe score of 2/10 and grey-zone financials, we need to qualify a second source for continuity — and since you pay suppliers at 105d while we're at 30, let's discuss moving us to 60 days to align working capital and keep the volume with you.
